# Mode2 acknowledged-publication guest preparation

This additive helper prepares only `postpublish-notify`, with the
`owner-published-hold-v1` controller and `runnable-thread-v1` payload. It derives
from the exact unchanged fault preparer retained beside this file; the complete
forward and inverse source diffs are retained too. Mode3 is rejected until its
separate eight-HELLO composition is reviewed and validated.

The source is prepared for independent review. It has not been imported,
compiled, executed, or used to prepare a root in the author's lane. No compiler,
QEMU, payload or test process is launched by the helper.

The exact new module record, its preparation2 record and the actual published
client test record are pinned by SHA-256 in the helper. The module's 63 retained
compiler bindings are joined to its historical compile identities, without
reading restored production source paths as if they were the overlay. The
complete unformatted source inventory is joined to preparation2. The original
19-case owner-parser proof is reused through preparation2's `fixture_inputs`;
the published build itself has a different fixture-input schema.

The actual client has paired `inputs` and `compiler_dependencies`, flat
`compiled_outputs`, and output `controller.elf`. The two exact controller/header
source hashes must match both retained source inputs and their compiler input
copies. The completed commands, exact output bytes and captured library
identities are checked. An unchanged old `fault-after-hello` utility remains an
inert inherited collection utility: this mode does not invoke it, and it provides
no version2 or mode3 evidence.

The original accepted gzip/newc archive must match the whole inherited root,
including byte/type/mode/link entries, apart from its two explicit device nodes.
The same image, launcher, runnable payload, auxiliary virtio module and exporter
are bound through their existing records. Every copied bound binary/library is
written from the bytes that were actually hashed. The observed input identities
are rechecked before completing preparation. The helper retains its own exact
source, the original preparer, every loaded record, copy bindings and final root
inventory. Failures remain in the fresh output tree with a FAIL record.

The final preparation status is `PREPARED_REQUIRES_COMPILED_STACK_REVIEW`.
`guest_release_ready`, guest/payload execution and every acceptance field remain
false. `compiled_stack_readiness` remains `PENDING_ACTUAL_REVIEW`, bound to the
exact module record and three module outputs. The separate coordinator must join
an independently reviewed actual compiled frame/chain readiness record before
any guest release. This helper neither changes the module's immutable
`actual_stack_frames_verified=false` nor claims a complete Linux stack bound.
Dynamic formatting/callback/kernel residuals belong to that separate review.

The prepared init uses STF2 through the new controller and version2 private
phase ioctl `0xc100f502`. It still derives OS/generation from the unique actual
boot record. Its original artifact-port name/device-number check, export-on-EXIT
and success-ACK-before-poweroff mechanism are preserved. Host code must bind the
actual prepared root, QEMU capture, physical/typed ownership, UART identities,
release digest, cleanup, and complete export; preparation alone proves none of
those runtime requirements.

The intended pinned-container command shape is below. The caller supplies a
fresh nonzero 32-hex nonce and a nonexistent canonical direct-child output under
`/work`; uid1000 and CPU affinity2–5 remain required. Run the repository helper
so its relative original-source fixture is present. These commands are a recipe,
not an author execution record.

```text
python3 /workspace/scripts/tests/prepare_stability_published_guest.py \
  --module /work/stability-published-hold-module-20260913-postpublish-notify-1 \
  --mode postpublish-notify --nonce <fresh-32-hex-nonce> \
  --controller-profile owner-published-hold-v1 \
  --payload-profile runnable-thread-v1 \
  --output /work/<fresh-mode2-preparation-name>
```
